Smt. Manne Bhudavva vs V. Anand Prasad And Another on 12
August, 2024
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 M.A.C.M.A No.3832 of 2012
Judgment:

entities.text: Manne Bhudavva vs V. Anand Prasad And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the award dated 08.05.2009 in O.P.No.782 of 2007 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-III Addl. District and Sessions Judge (FTC) at Medak, the claimant has preferred this appeal.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-III Addl. District and Sessions Judge (FTC) at Medak
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard both sides and perused the entire material on record.
3.
The claimant is married daughter of deceased.
She has filed the claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- and the Tribunal has granted Rs.60,000/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization.

4. According to version of the claimant, on 06.07.2007, while the deceased was crossing the road along with others, the offending vehicle which is a bus driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner hit the deceased, resulting in her death.

The Tribunal having found that the claimant is married daughter of the deceased and not dependant on the deceased, has not calculated the amount under the head of loss of dependency and granted an amount of Rs.50,000/- under no fault liability.
Apart from that, only an amount of Rs.2,000/- towards cremation charges and Rs.8,000/- towards loss of love and affection were granted.

Learned counsel relied on the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in G. Narayanappa and another v. Government of Andhra Pradesh1 and Manjuri Bera (Smt) v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.2 to buttress his arguments that married daughter can also claim compensation.

entities.text: G. Narayanappa and another v. Government of Andhra Pradesh1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manjuri Bera (Smt) v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. The Tribunal having considered the manner in which the accident has taken place and also finding that the driver of the offending vehicle is liable, however erred in granting compensation as No fault liability compensation.

Once the Tribunal comes to the conclusion that the vehicle was at fault resulting in the accident and subsequent death, the 1992 AIR 135 (2007) 10 SCC 643 KS, J MACMA_3832_2012 compensation ought to be granted according to the income of the deceased.
7. As per the claimant, the deceased was earning an amount of Rs.60/- to Rs.70/- by doing cooli work.
Hence, this Court is inclined to consider the monthly income at Rs.1,800/- and grant compensation.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 3 has held that while considering the compensation in cases of death, the future prospects of the self employed shall also be considered.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having regard to the age of deceased as 46 years as on the date of accident and occupation as self-employed, if 25 percent of the income is included as future prospects, the monthly income would come to Rs.2,250/- (Rs.1,800+450).

If 1/3rd of the income is deducted towards personal expenditure, as per the authority in Smt. Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation4, thus the annual contribution of the deceased to the claimant would be Rs.18,000/-
(Rs.2,250-750X12).

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Schedule II of the Act, 2017 (6) 170 (SC) (2009) 6 S.C.C. 121 KS, J MACMA_3832_2012 if the said annual contribution arrived is multiplied with relevant multiplier to the age of the deceased i.e. '13', the total amount comes to Rs.2,34,000/-.
The claimant is entitled for the said amount under the head of loss of dependency.

9. Under the head of loss of love and affection, the Tribunal has granted an amount of Rs.8,000/-
and this Court is not inclined to interfere with the said finding.
10. Relying on the ratio laid down in case of Pranay Sethi (3 supra), the claimant is granted Rs.30,000/- towards funeral expenses.

11. Therefore, the claimant is eligible for the compensation as below:
 Head Compensation awarded  (1) Loss of dependency Rs.2,34,000  (2) Funeral expenses and Loss of Estate Rs.30,000  (3) Loss of love and affection Rs.8,000

Total compensation awarded Rs.2,72,000/-
 KS, J  MACMA_3832_2012 12.
In the result, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.60,000/- to Rs.2,72,000/-.
(a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(b) The respondents shall deposit the amount within a period of (8) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of judgment.
On such deposit, claimant is entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing the security.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
No order as to costs.

4. According to version of the claimant, on 06.07.2007, while the deceased was crossing the road along with others, the offending vehicle which is a bus driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner hit the deceased, resulting in her death.
The Tribunal having found that the claimant is married daughter of the deceased and not dependant on the deceased, has not calculated the amount under the head of loss of dependency and granted an amount of Rs.50,000/- under no fault liability.
Once the Tribunal comes to the conclusion that the vehicle was at fault resulting in the accident and subsequent death, the 1992 AIR 135 (2007) 10 SCC 643 KS, J MACMA_3832_2012 compensation ought to be granted according to the income of the deceased.
opennyai_summary.arguments: Learned counsel relied on the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in G. Narayanappa and another v. Government of Andhra Pradesh1 and Manjuri Bera (Smt) v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.2 to buttress his arguments that married daughter can also claim compensation.
opennyai_summary.issue: 6. The Tribunal having considered the manner in which the accident has taken place and also finding that the driver of the offending vehicle is liable, however erred in granting compensation as No fault liability compensation.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 3 has held that while considering the compensation in cases of death, the future prospects of the self employed shall also be considered.
If 1/3rd of the income is deducted towards personal expenditure, as per the authority in Smt. Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation4, thus the annual contribution of the deceased to the claimant would be Rs.18,000/-
(Rs.2,250-750X12).

As per Schedule II of the Act, 2017 (6) 170 (SC) (2009) 6 S.C.C. 121 KS, J MACMA_3832_2012 if the said annual contribution arrived is multiplied with relevant multiplier to the age of the deceased i.e. '13', the total amount comes to Rs.2,34,000/-.

and this Court is not inclined to interfere with the said finding.
10. Relying on the ratio laid down in case of Pranay Sethi (3 supra), the claimant is granted Rs.30,000/- towards funeral expenses.

Total compensation awarded Rs.2,72,000/-

In the result, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.60,000/- to Rs.2,72,000/-.
(a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(b) The respondents shall deposit the amount within a period of (8) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of judgment.
On such deposit, claimant is entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing the security.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
